The addendum ends: *Money is not the only thing characters carry. They carry obligations. They carry evidence. They carry debts that never appear on a sheet.*

Waluigi will now inventory what the Feyward branch is carrying, since nobody else has.

**Obligations.** A ring lodged with the Anvil containing, allegedly, a person. A construct's remains that were promised burial rather than salvage. A Toad who is either a victim or a vector and has been told he is neither.

**Evidence.** Everything in this file. Twelve exhibits, in custody, with hands attached to each one.

**Debts that never appear on a sheet.** Morel is owed something for the key, and Morel will name the price at a moment of Morel's choosing. Akamatsu is owed 650 gold and has not pressed. [[roll:4|Aurelian is owed her body back|and the debt is owed by the party, who currently hold her in a ring, filed under Article, lodged with a smith.|owed by someone. The file does not say who.]].

None of that is on a quest board because a quest board cannot represent it. It is on this page because Waluigi's archive can, and because a debt that has been written down is considerably harder to walk away from than a debt that has merely been felt.

exhibits.title: Threshold note — Green T after the storm line
exhibits.secured: 30 Harvestide, 1040 BF · filed from overlapping witness accounts at Tymnas's cottage
exhibits.visual: FOREHEAD ONLY
exhibits.onRecord: Green T returned from the storm line and failed the cottage's comfort test immediately. He was challenged as a possible fake, answered with a gunshot through freshly repaired glass, and then glowed under Markop's blood-sense [[roll:4|only at the forehead|localized contamination is a touch, a seal, or an embedded thing. Whole-body falsehood would have been simpler and more dangerous in a different way.|the spell may simply have caught residue in the rain and nothing more.]].
exhibits.analysis:
## The useful part is where the spell stopped

Whole-body failure would have made this easy. The spell did not do that. It lit the forehead only, which means the archive is looking at a mark, not a replacement. Marks can be acquired. Replacements are a different bureaucracy.

## The threshold was opened by impatience, not certainty

Remi said no and was correct on the merits. Markop was too exhausted to resolve the question. Eager let Green T in because deadlock had become more dangerous than risk. [[roll:5|That is still a decision structure, not an accident|the cottage did not blunder. It delegated under fatigue, which is the sort of sentence armies use shortly before writing memorials.|fatigue is chaos with polite wording.]]. The archive should treat the admission as chosen and therefore analyzable.

## Mazebound is not an answer, only a direction

Green T's own explanation — that the residue was Mazebound and that he got what he needed — narrows the map without reducing the fear. It tells the file where to look next and nothing about what followed him back. That is enough to keep the lead open.

exhibits.title: Receipt — Remi armed up before the floor moved
exhibits.secured: 30 Harvestide, 1040 BF · preserved from Wario's table during the storm watch
exhibits.visual: THREE ITEMS · ONE STORM
exhibits.onRecord: The receipt is not about price so much as timing. Remi bought three items while the cottage was still deciding whether its shelter counted as shelter. [[roll:3|Wario kept selling through the crisis instead of after it|which means he judged the danger as negotiable long before anybody else did. Wario's sense for survivable disaster remains offensively sharp.|Wario sells through everything. That is personality, not field intelligence.]].
exhibits.analysis:
## A market judgment disguised as a receipt

A receipt proves somebody thought there would still be a later in which money mattered. That is the hidden optimism of commerce, and Wario was optimistic enough to finish the lines properly while the weather argued with the walls.

## Weapon choice as mood ring

Skullsplitter Warhammer. Peach's Castle Brick. The Rotting Skull Piercer. Not food, not rope, not nails, not blankets. The cottage bought impact. [[roll:4|That tells the archive how the room felt before Green T knocked|the shopping list is a fear profile: hit back, throw something heavy, carry one thing too horrible for ordinary use. Nobody in that room believed rest was next.|people buy whatever Wario has in front of them. Lists flatter analysts.]].

## The free decoy remains off-book

The decoy crystal matters partly because the receipt does not dignify it with a line. Off-book help from Wario is help he intends to remember as leverage, not as inventory. The archive notes the omission and keeps moving.

exhibits.title: Six names, one struck through, nobody's signature
exhibits.secured: 1 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) · lifted off the map table before the wood came through the wall
exhibits.custody: Archive copy — Waluigi made the list in eleven seconds
exhibits.visual: SIX NAMED · ONE STRUCK · UNSIGNED
exhibits.onRecord: The commission is written on the reverse of a barrel tally, which is the paper the house had left. [[roll:3|strength: six, one struck through|the tally was struck BEFORE the roll call, which means whoever wrote it knew a man was dead and counted him anyway. Somebody in the war room was doing arithmetic on the living and the dead at the same time, and did not tell the dwarf.|a struck line is bookkeeping. Staff strike lines all day.]] There is no signature. The authority line reads *the map master, O.C.* and nothing else.
exhibits.analysis:
## Authority in this house is furniture

Nobody signed this. The commission says it comes from the map master and the map master comes from two initials, and two initials in this family have already been found carved into bedframes and struck onto soul-capture hardware. [[roll:4|That is the graft, running in daylight|the same move the file opened on — take an existing authority, do not sign anything, and let the object carry the weight. A commission nobody signed cannot be traced to a person, only to a table.|initials are everywhere in this family. Proximity is not authorship.]]

## The struck line is the honest part

Two men were dead before the roll call and the paper still says strength: six. That is not a lie; it is a document written to a number somebody upstairs wanted to see.

## One trade on the list is *waiter*

Brad. A waiter, in a combat detachment, because the house had spent its guards on the foyer and its fairies on the music. The archive files this under what a manor looks like on its fourth day.

exhibits.title: An evacuation signed by the thing being evacuated from
exhibits.secured: 1 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) · taken from a house guard on the east stair, mid-shout
exhibits.visual: ORDER OF THE REVEL · SEALED
exhibits.onRecord: The order moves civilians to the upper flowers, tells them not to open the drink doors, and says the music will resume. [[roll:3|The Revel is issuing safety orders about itself|a thing that has to warn a house not to interrupt it is a thing that can be interrupted. The order is an admission, filed as a courtesy.|safety notices are boilerplate. Every office writes them.]] Every fairy on that stair obeyed it without a single question.
exhibits.analysis:
## Total authority does not need to be enforced

Nobody argued with this paper. Not the drunk half, not the sober half, not the satyr who wanted to join the trees. The order was shouted by one guard on one stair and the whole floor moved.

## The resume clause

[[roll:5|Attendance will be resumed when the floors are safe|the Revel plans to keep going after the house is repaired. It is not a siege, it is a schedule. The library volume said the only endings are total surrender or somebody willing to be the one who stopped the music — and this paper is the Revel saying it has read the same book.|the clause could be politeness. Offices promise continuity reflexively.]]

## Why the party did not simply obey

Hjumpik went the other way on this order. The archive files that as the second time in one week he has refused a route offered by something more powerful than him.

exhibits.title: One page, headed TECHNICAL
exhibits.secured: 1 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) · written in the corridor, four minutes after the argument
exhibits.custody: Waluigi's own hand — filed at the other man's suggestion
exhibits.visual: ONE PAGE · UNDERLINED TWICE
exhibits.onRecord: The leaf transcribes the argument word for word and underlines one word twice. [[roll:3|The transcript was written within four minutes|Waluigi wrote it while the dwarf was still walking away, which means the page is a contemporaneous record and not a recollection. In a dispute about who is in charge, that is the only piece of paper either of them will ever have.|he keeps a notebook. Notebooks get written in.]] The plea is recorded in full, including the part about the ritual.
exhibits.analysis:
## A plea, on the record, at last

The planar fracture ritual has been in this file since it opened. What has never been on paper is that Waluigi asked, out loud, before it happened, and was not listened to. [[roll:4|The dwarf did not deny it|he said *it's not just that* and moved on to the plant monsters. That is not a denial, it is a deferral, and deferrals in this house have a way of becoming the answer.|deflection under pressure proves nothing about the underlying claim.]]

## Who is actually in command

Technically the dwarf. Practically the archivist, whenever the dwarf is wrong, which the same page records the dwarf conceding in advance. That is not a chain of command. That is a friendship with a tiebreaker.

## Why the paper exists at all

Hjumpik told him to write it down as a way of ending the argument. The archive notes that the argument did end, and the paper did not.

exhibits.title: Dinner service sheet - the third course has no price
exhibits.secured: 2 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) · taken from the kitchen prep table
exhibits.visual:
I — broth · hall & posts
II — root and barley · hall
III — the green dish · overgrowth only
IV — dessert · held back
NO COST ENTERED · LINE III
exhibits.onRecord: Four courses. Three of them are priced to the copper. [[roll:3|the third course carries no cost against it|a kitchen this meticulous does not forget a price; a blank in an otherwise complete ledger means the item was never bought, but made from something the house already had or from something nobody wants written down|a standing dish repeated nightly can simply be costed once, elsewhere, in a stores book this sheet does not duplicate]] The third course is also the only one with a delivery restriction: to the overgrowth only, do not carry to the hall, do not taste. [[roll:4|do not let the sprites carry it, they eat from the tray|somebody has already thought about friendly casualties and written a control into the standing order, which makes this an operation with a safety procedure rather than a desperate improvisation|kitchens keep sprites off trays as ordinary practice, poison or no poison]]
exhibits.analysis:
## The manor's only working weapon is a menu

Everything else in this file is a plan. The heir has a map with pins in it. Hjumpik has a marching order. The Revel has an evacuation notice nobody can enforce. Red has a **delivery system the enemy already trusts**, running on a schedule the house has never stopped keeping.

That is the entire finding. The overgrowth cannot be cut faster than it grows — the wall walk proved that when the cut leaves came back thicker inside a minute. It can, apparently, be **fed**. And a great house at war still serves dinner, so the vector was always going to be the one service that never stops.

What the sheet adds beyond the scene is the discipline. *Do not let the sprites carry it — they eat from the tray.* Somebody has already thought about friendly casualties and written a control into the standing order. This is not a desperate improvisation by a cook. It is an operation with a safety procedure.

The open question is authorisation. The sheet is **unsigned**, and Red's first words to the party were *did orange guy send you* — which is not the question of someone acting under the heir's orders. Either the heir knows and has kept it off paper, or the manor's most effective counter-attack is being run by its kitchen without anybody upstairs being told.

exhibits.title: Three reasons to trust me, offered without hesitation
exhibits.secured: 2 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) · the lower hall, before the hidden door was opened
exhibits.visual:
1. Aurelian is helping
2. Orangus Cornelius
3. I stopped Wario
OFFERED IN THIS ORDER
exhibits.onRecord: Asked why he should be trusted, the guard produced three credentials on his fingers without pausing to think. [[roll:4|he had all three ready|a man assembles a defence in advance when he expects to be challenged, so either somebody in this house has already asked him or he has been waiting for somebody to|a guard on a hidden door is challenged constantly and would rehearse an answer as a matter of routine]] He then opened a hidden door with three knocks that Hjumpik had been taught and could not reproduce. [[roll:3|bloodshot eyes over an insistence that the mushroom room did nothing to him|the room has an effect its own guards deny and the mushrooms themselves do not carry, which means the agent is something else in that room and the fungus is what everyone is looking at|a guard at the end of a long shift in a smoky lower hall has bloodshot eyes for ordinary reasons]]
exhibits.analysis:
## Every credential is borrowed, and one of them is a name nobody says

Taken one at a time:

**Aurelian is helping.** She is folded into a gold band in Hjumpik's pocket and has helped nobody for weeks. Either he does not know that, which makes him badly informed for a man with a hidden door, or he is using her name the way people use a patron's name — as borrowed standing.

**Orangus Cornelius.** This is the load-bearing one. It is the name the Guard With No Name refused to let the false Lady finish saying, the name a defector gave up his post rather than pronounce. This guard offers it as a **reference**, in a corridor, unprompted. Two men in the same household have opposite relationships with one name, and the difference between them is the shape of whatever faction exists inside this house.

**I stopped Wario.** A claim available to anybody, made by many, evidenced by none.

Set that against the two facts he did not intend to give away: bloodshot eyes over an insistence that the mushroom room did nothing to him, and *I didn't think you would come back that soon* — the sentence of a man who had budgeted more time for something. He is not lying about being useful. He opened the door. The door went in a circle, which may be the house's decision rather than his.

exhibits.title: The denial was testable, and nobody tested it for three filings
exhibits.secured: 30 Harvestide, 1040 BF · from beneath the subject, mid-engagement
exhibits.custody: Waluigi's own hand — no sample, no face recovered
exhibits.visual:
STATED (×3): I am not a monster
FILED (×3): monster
TESTED (×1): human blood
RANGE: ZERO INCHES
exhibits.onRecord: Pinned under the fallen subject, Remi Akamatsu observed that she was at point-blank range and discharged a musket into its face. The face came off and the blood beneath it was human. [[roll:3|the subject had made the same claim on three prior filed occasions|a creature that repeats one specific denial across three engagements is not taunting, it is correcting the record, and the party has been arguing with a thing that keeps telling them what it is|monsters in this archive say theatrical things constantly and the repetition proves only that it has a favourite line]] The subject did not press the advantage after being unmasked. It laughed and withdrew into the mouth of its own tree. [[roll:5|it left immediately after the face came off, not after the wound|the exposure was the intolerable event rather than the injury, which means the face is doing work — concealment, or restraint, or both|a creature knocked down, sliced by a shadow blade and shot in the head has ordinary reasons to disengage without any of them being about identity]]
exhibits.analysis:
## Three filings of the archive calling something a liar for telling the truth

The method here is worth naming, because the file has seen it before under another heading. **Whoever keeps the record decides afterwards what happened** — and what happened, on the record, is that a creature stated a fact four times and the record printed the word *monster* in the same paragraph on every occasion.

That is not a small error of tone. Every operational decision this party made about the Scorncrow followed from the classification. Garlic weapons. An **anti-fey elixir**, bought and drunk, purchased specifically for bonus attacks against *fey, undead, and other monsters*. A wizard's repeated attempts to uproot it as though it were vegetation. A plan whose stated objective was to *uproot the belly of the beast*. Every one of those is a countermeasure selected for a category, and the category was chosen by the archivist rather than by the evidence.

Set the elixir against the finding and the arithmetic gets uncomfortable: if the blood is human, the squad's consumable edge was optimised against a thing the subject may not be, and the fact that the fights still went badly stops being mysterious.

**What the finding does not settle.** Human blood under a scarecrow's face admits at least three readings, and this file will not choose between them on one observation taken by a fourteen-year-old under a corpse's weight with no sample retained:

- **Worn.** Something human is inside the construct, willingly or not.
- **Made.** Something human *was* made into the construct — in which case *I am not a monster* is a complaint, filed four times, in a grove whose interior boughs are hung with wrapped people.
- **Costumed.** The blood is a further layer, laid on by something that has watched this party for three engagements and worked out what would stop them.

The third reading deserves more respect than it is comfortable to give it, because the subject's behaviour inside the tree — attacking the motorbike before the man — is the behaviour of something that studies.

**Where it connects.** The graft thread in this file already holds a document arguing that what is joined is not the flesh but the line, and that a line joined once can be joined again. A human interior under a non-human exterior is that vocabulary in a different medium. The file is not asserting the connection. It is refusing to pretend it cannot see it.

exhibits.title: Two men solved the same door and both solutions closed it
exhibits.secured: 30 Harvestide, 1040 BF · set at the jaws before the rope went down
exhibits.visual:
1 Feyward Dan · paladin
2 Eager
3 Archie · squishy
4 Salam
5 Markop · rope
DESCENT BY ROPE · DEPTH UNKNOWN
exhibits.onRecord: Archie's all-in fire cast killed the tree and sealed the exit. Markop then removed a piece of bark intending to widen the way, and the jaws shut. [[roll:4|every intervention made the opening smaller|a structure that closes further each time it is worked on is not a door failing, it is a mechanism succeeding, and the party has been operating the wrong end of it|a dying tree collapsing inward under fire and structural damage is the least surprising thing in this file]] The order that followed was set with a stated reason against each position, the only decision of the session filed that way. [[roll:6|the reasoning survives but the condition of the marchers does not appear in it|the order was written for a party that no longer existed — two of the five had spent every point of magic they had before the first step down|a marching order records position, not readiness, and expecting a condition report inside one is asking a rope plan to be a medical file]]
exhibits.analysis:
## A throat, and five people who wrote a good plan for the wrong party

**On the structure.** Take the sequence at face value, because it is short and it is consistent. Fire bolt: bark scarred, nothing. Second bolt: nothing. Full expenditure: the tree dies and the exit seals. Bark plate removed: the jaws shut. Torch dropped into the pit: the torch comes back out of the trunk.

Five interventions, five closures, and one of them returned an object by a route the party did not use. A door that jams is a door. A structure that answers every kind of pressure by closing, and that can push something back out through a different part of itself, is doing something else. The plainest reading available is that the party is not besieging a building; they have been swallowed, and the model that fits the observations is digestion rather than fortification.

**On the order.** This is the best piece of work in the session and the file should be honest about why it still failed. Markop wrote position with justification attached — paladin at the front, the wizard in the middle because the wizard is squishy, the centaur at the rear because the rope is his. Nothing in it is wrong.

What is missing is the column the party needed most. Position one had spent every point of magic he owned healing himself. Position three had spent every point of his emptying it into the tree. Two of five were at zero, both of them had said so out loud within the previous ten minutes, and the order records neither fact. The plan was correct for the party that walked into the grove and was written for the party that walked out of it.

**Consequence for the file.** The exit is not a lead about getting home; it is a lead about how the Legion got in. Something is inside a structure with one mouth that had to be pried apart by a centaur's hands. Either the closure is selective, or there is a second opening. Both answers are worth more than the rope.

exhibits.title: The pit answered, in the plural, and only one person heard it
exhibits.secured: 30 Harvestide, 1040 BF · both sides of the trunk, same moment
exhibits.custody: Archive — two accounts, one witness each
exhibits.visual:
OUTSIDE: torch in → torch out
INSIDE: they're going to burn
— us all down
SOUNDING FAILED · ANSWER RECEIVED
exhibits.onRecord: A torch was thrown into the pit to measure it. Outside, the torch came back out of the trunk and the sounding returned nothing. Inside, Remi Akamatsu heard voices: *there's a fire, someone is causing a fire, they're going to burn us all down.* [[roll:3|the objection is grammatical, collective and correctly reasoned|whatever is in there can hear, can speak, can identify a fire as a fire and can refer to itself as a group, which puts a population in the pit rather than a hazard|panicked speech carries in a confined space and a few intelligible words prove intelligence in the speaker, not numbers]] The torch returned by a route the party did not throw it down. [[roll:5|it came out of the trunk, not the jaws|the interior has at least one opening the party has not found, which is also the likeliest answer to how a Legion detachment reached ground with no marched route|an object thrown into a pit inside a hollow tree can be pushed back up any number of ways by anything strong enough, and no second opening is required]]
exhibits.analysis:
## Somebody in there said *us*

**The word doing all the work is a pronoun.** Not *me*, not a scream, not noise. *They're going to burn us all down.* That single word converts the pit from a hazard into a population, and it does it with grammar the party never asked for and cannot have supplied.

Work out what the sentence requires of its speakers. They perceived a fire. They identified it as deliberate — *someone is causing a fire*. They inferred an intention held by parties outside a wall they cannot see through. And they described themselves as a plural body with a shared fate. That is four cognitive operations, performed under stress, by things the party has been calling scenery.

**Set it beside the inner grove and the reading gets worse.** The heart of the Skittering Grove is hung with the forms of wrapped creatures, beast and man, dangling from the boughs like fruit. The file is not going to assert that the wrapped are the speakers, because one witness heard voices through wood and nobody has cut anything down. But the archive holds a location with hanging people in it and a recording of people in that location objecting to being burned, and it would be a strange kind of rigour to file those on separate pages and never mention it.

**What it costs the party.** Archie's fire cast was the largest single expenditure of the night, and the fire it answered is the fire those voices were already panicking about — the test torch, thrown minutes earlier. From inside, the sequence reads: a fire arrives, they raise the alarm, and then a wizard empties his reserves into the walls. Whatever is in that grove now has a first impression of this party, and it is arson.

**The plainer finding, and the one worth acting on.** The torch came back out of the trunk. It went in at the jaws. Something moved an object between two openings, and the party only knows about one of them.

exhibits.title: The manor's dead reinforcements were killed with edged weapons, and only the unrelieved guard noticed
exhibits.secured: 2 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) · the hallway post, from a guard who was never debriefed
exhibits.custody: Archive — single witness, uncorroborated, unpursued by anybody present
exhibits.visual:
CAUSE OF DEATH — REINFORCEMENT DETAIL
expected: crush / engulf / rot
observed: sword slashes
ONE WITNESS · NO FOLLOW-UP
exhibits.onRecord: A house guard, still holding a hallway nobody has relieved him from, was asked what happened to the reinforcements. He said they died. Asked whether the plants killed them, he said: *not from plants, from other people, they had sword slashes.* [[roll:3|the overgrowth does not carry edged weapons|every vegetation casualty in three sessions of filings presents as crushing, engulfing or rot; the treants club and throw bark, the mound engulfs, the fungus rots, and none of them cut|a panicking guard describing wounds he saw briefly in poor light is not a coroner, and torn bark-strike wounds on soft tissue can look like anything you already expect to see]] The same guard, told that the kitchen's cooking withers the overgrowth on contact, proposed loading it into a bomb. [[roll:5|the man holding the corridor is also the only one running the problem|three sessions of planning rooms, war tables and marching orders have produced no weapon test; the unrelieved sentry produced a delivery mechanism in one sentence, which says something uncomfortable about where this household keeps its thinking|it is an obvious idea and obvious ideas occur to everybody; the reason nobody built it is that nobody has a bomb specialist, not that nobody thought of it]]
exhibits.analysis:
## There is a second killer in this house and it uses a sword

**The file has been prosecuting the wrong case.** Every page in this arc treats the Overgrown Manor as a siege by vegetation: one hostile, many bodies, a plant problem with a plant solution. The hallway guard's sentence breaks that frame in nine words, and the archive is going to treat it as a break rather than as colour.

The evidentiary value is in the *mismatch*, not the wound. A witness who wanted to be useful would have said the plants did it — that is the answer the house is primed for, the answer his officers expect, and the answer that requires no further conversation. He gave the inconvenient answer instead, unprompted, to a dwarf who was not his superior and who had not asked a leading question. Testimony that costs the witness something is worth more than testimony that costs him nothing, and this cost him the rest of his shift being wrong in front of strangers.

**Who is holding a sword in this building.** The manor's own guards carry heavy crossbows and quarterstaves; the ledger from the Revel room logs them firing bolts at a hundred feet, not cutting. The Satyr Swordfighter carries a scimitar and, over three rounds, put eight multiattacks into the *House Guard* — not into the treant. The Satyr Rogue carries shortswords and spent its entire engagement stabbing the Satyr Bard. The file notes, without yet asserting, that the two combatants in this house who are armed with blades are also the two combatants who spent the engagement killing the house and its own.

**Against that reading.** A fey Revel that has been drinking for three sessions and has now had its party invaded does not need to be infiltrated to start swinging at the wrong people. Chaos is the Revel's native state. The archive has repeatedly mistaken fey indifference for fey conspiracy and has had to amend the filing afterwards.

**What decides it.** Nobody has examined a body. Not one. Three sessions, a mounting casualty list, and the only forensic observation in the entire file came from a man who was not asked and was not listened to. The lead is not *who has a sword* — it is *go and look at the dead*.

exhibits.title: The thing wearing Lady Aurelian answered to a word nobody had used as a name
exhibits.secured: 2 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) · the sealed sanctuary, doors vined shut, one witness inside
exhibits.custody: Hjumpik Deldkur — sole witness; recorded to the archive immediately after
exhibits.visual:
“plants are carnivorous, right—”
“that…. my name…..”
NAME OBTAINED · NOT SOUGHT
exhibits.onRecord: Hjumpik, stalling inside a sealed room, asked the false Aurelian twice whether the plant it was sitting on was a good plant to sit on, then said *plants are carnivorous, right—*. The thing replied, with pauses transcribed as heard: *that's.... my name.....* [[roll:4|a fey answered to a true name by accident and then stopped talking about it|it did not correct him, did not laugh, and did not continue the sentence it had been enjoying; a creature that has held a perfect impersonation through three sessions of conversation dropped its cadence on one word, which is the behaviour of a name and not of a vocabulary error|it is a plant creature being condescended to about botany by a dwarf; 'that's my name' is exactly the sort of flat joke a thing makes when a mortal explains its own biology to it, and the pauses are menace, not malfunction]] Immediately before the slip it had volunteered its entire strategy unprompted: rule the manor, let the manor collapse, trees grow anew, *the beauty of nature is slow*. [[roll:6|the confession and the slip are the same failure|it talked freely because it had already sealed the doors and counted the room as won; the same confidence that produced a full statement of intent produced an unguarded answer to a name, and both are artefacts of a creature that stopped performing once it believed nobody would be leaving|a monster monologuing before it wins is the oldest behaviour in the archive and proves nothing about what its name is]]
exhibits.analysis:
## A name is the only thing in this arc that can be acted on

**Everything else this file holds about the overgrowth is descriptive.** It grows. It impersonates. It withers when fed Red's cooking. None of that is leverage. A name, in the Feyward, is a different category of object entirely, and the file has to decide how much weight to put on five syllables spoken with ellipses in them.

**The case for taking it seriously starts with what preceded it.** Hjumpik was not conducting an interrogation. He was talking about *furniture* — an absurd, sustained, deliberately trivial line about whether it is bad manners to sit on a flower — and he ran it twice, which is the part that matters. The first pass got a straight answer (*it's just a foflower*). The second pass got *hmmm, what do you mean*. The creature had stopped tracking the conversation as an attack, which is precisely when the word landed.

**The competing reading deserves its due.** Fey are fond of flat, affectless jokes, and *that's my name* is a serviceable one. This file has been embarrassed before by treating fey wordplay as a revelation. If the archive stakes an action on a name that turns out to be a pun, it will have handed a creature that plans in months a way to waste the party's only remaining session.

**What tips it.** The transcription. Hjumpik recorded pauses — *that's.... my name.....* — and pauses are the thing a joke does not have. A joke lands on the beat. This did not land; it trailed, and then the conversation did not go back to it, and a creature that had answered every other question in the room at length declined to expand on this one. The overgrowth explained its objective, its timetable, and its reason for wearing a dead woman's face, and the only subject it would not elaborate on was its own name.

**Practical consequence.** Red's dinner damages it physically; the file already knows that. What the file did not have until now is anything to *bind* it with. Every fey instrument in this campaign — the soul ring, the bell, the Accords' own language about bound objects — runs on names. The party is carrying a ring that holds a person and a bell that has done something inexplicable twice, and it now has a name to put in front of both.

exhibits.title: Forty-four turns in which the Revel's best fighters attacked their own side
exhibits.secured: 2 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) · the Revel room, three rounds, logged in full
exhibits.visual:
Swordfighter → House Guard ×8
Sorcerer → Swordfighter ×4
Rogue → Bard ×3
Druid → Swordfighter
3 ROUNDS · 44 TURNS · NO DECISION
exhibits.onRecord: Three rounds, forty-four NPC turns, twenty-four attack actions and thirteen spells produced no decision. The Satyr Swordfighter, busiest combatant in the room, spent eight multiattacks on the House Guard. The Satyr Sorcerer spent four spells on the Satyr Swordfighter. The Satyr Rogue put a hand crossbow and two shortswords into the Satyr Bard. [[roll:4|this is not a melee getting confused, it is a pattern with direction|the same attackers returned to the same targets round after round, and morale stayed BOLD in the eighties throughout; troops who have lost cohesion break or scatter, they do not calmly re-engage the same friendly target for three consecutive rounds|a fey revel is not a military unit and was never cohesive; expecting formation discipline from a party that has been drinking for three sessions is a category error]] Meanwhile the Treant cast Animate Trees twice, adding combatants that act on its own initiative count. [[roll:3|the treant was not trying to win the fight|it spent its actions reproducing rather than killing while everything else in the room spent its actions on everything else in the room, which is what an organism does when it is not in danger|it is a plant with two actions and a multiattack; using one on summoning is ordinary monster tactics and implies no strategy at all]]
exhibits.analysis:
## A faction attacking itself, or a faction already taken

**The interesting number is not forty-four. It is eight.** Eight multiattacks from the single most active combatant in the room, every one of them aimed at the manor's own House Guard, while a treant stood in the middle of the floor growing more treants. If the Revel were merely chaotic, the targeting would be *scattered* — it is not. Each attacker returned to the same target across rounds. That is selection, and selection has a cause.

**Morale forecloses the easiest explanation.** The ledger stamps morale readings throughout: BOLD, in the eighties, for almost every combatant, round after round. Panic produces flight and mis-targeting; it does not produce confident, repeated, accurate engagement of a chosen friendly. Whatever the Satyr Swordfighter thought it was doing, it was not frightened, and it did not change its mind.

**Set it against the upstairs finding.** The party established, in the same session, that the lady of the manor is a plant wearing a dead woman, that it has been moving pieces into position deliberately, and that it is patient on a scale of months. A creature with that much control over the household's chain of command does not need to fight the Revel. It needs the Revel pointed at the house.

**The honest counterweight.** No compulsion effect was observed, named, or saved against. The ledger shows Sleep, Colour Spray, Mockery and Thunderwave — nothing that dominates. If some of these fey are controlled, the mechanism is not in this log, and a file that concludes control from targeting alone is guessing with a table of numbers in front of it to look rigorous.

**What the file will say.** Not that the Revel is compromised. That the Revel can no longer be counted as an ally in planning, because on the evidence of three full rounds it cannot be predicted to attack the enemy, and a party that plans an ambush around it is planning around a variable it does not control.

exhibits.title: The only paperwork the execution produced
exhibits.secured: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF · Skittering Grove, after the swing
exhibits.visual: CONDITION OF PRIOR HOLDER · KNEELING
exhibits.onRecord: One scythe, of stolen origin, transferred from the Scorncrow to Markop in the Skittering Grove on 1 Aethel, 1040 BF. The ledger records the prior holder as disarmed, kneeling and unmasked, and the cause of death as a single warhammer strike to the skull.
exhibits.analysis:
## An inventory line is the wrong shape for this

The entry is correct in every particular and it is still the wrong document. It has a field for the item, a field for who took it, and a field for the condition of the prior holder — and into that last field somebody has written **kneeling**, which is a word about a killing wearing the costume of a word about stock. [[roll:3|read the condition field as testimony|the transfer is recorded as happening AFTER the weapon was released, which means the scythe was not taken in a fight — it was picked up off the ground beside a body that had already surrendered it|the field records posture at the moment of transfer and cannot establish what was in anybody's mind]].

## What the ledger declines to record

There is no field on this form for *was an appeal made*, and so the appeal — the four words the thing said across four engagements, said again in the form of a request, to a paladin, by name — survives here only as a quotation with a note attached. [[roll:4|the quoted line is load-bearing|the archive's own ledger preserves the request while offering no place to record the answer, which is itself the answer: nothing was granted, because nothing was considered|the quotation is transcribed from party account and the wording of a dying sentence is the least reliable thing in any record]].

Waluigi files the object and refuses to file the verdict. The scythe is Markop's. What it cost is not written on any line of this.

exhibits.title: Two tests of one sentence, both of which it passed
exhibits.secured: 30 Harvestide 1040 and 1 Aethel 1040 · Skittering Grove
exhibits.custody: Archive observation note; no physical specimen retained
exhibits.visual: NOT ICHOR · NOT SAP · NOT SMOKE
exhibits.onRecord: On 30 Harvestide 1040 a point-blank musket shot removed the Scorncrow's face and the blood beneath it was human. On 1 Aethel 1040, in the grove, the hood came off and the face underneath was human and speaking. At death the remains stayed remains.
exhibits.analysis:
## The claim was testable and it was tested twice

For three filings the archive read *I am not a monster* as villain theatre, and Waluigi wrote that reading himself, which is why he is the one correcting it. Two independent physical tests, eleven days apart, by different means, returned the same result. [[roll:3|the physical record is consistent|two separate encounters produced human blood and a human face, and the body did not dissolve, burn off or revert at death the way every other constructed thing in this arc has|consistency between two party accounts is not the same as a specimen, and no specimen was kept]].

## Three readings, and the grove closed the door on all of them

Something human inside the scarecrow. Something human *made into* it. Or a monster that learned to bleed convincingly because it learned what this party would find persuasive. [[roll:5|the third reading is the weakest|a deception maintained through death, with no observer left to deceive and nothing further to gain, is a deception with no audience — which is not how deceptions work|a thing willing to die in costume is exactly the thing a sufficiently patient deceiver would build, and the archive has met patient things in this arc before]].

**The plain fact, unhedged:** the question was answerable right up until the swing. A disarmed, kneeling, unmasked prisoner who is talking is the most informative object anybody in this arc has ever had, and the party converted it into a body and a secondhand scythe. Waluigi is not moralising about the kill. He is filing the cost of it, which is that the archive now has three readings and no way left to choose.

exhibits.title: The Oracle's account of the assassination
exhibits.secured: uncorroborated
exhibits.custody: Waluipedia, via Bowser's retelling — no independent witness, no physical copy
exhibits.visual:
🕯️
Uncorroborated testimony
Highsun 1, 955 BF
recounted 922 BF
one comb, unsourced
exhibits.onRecord: Five or six mages' locks broken. The room untouched. Peach seated with a comb in her hand, dead, unmoving, blood on the floor. The responding guards came in and all died. Delivered unprompted, immediately after an hour of escalating provocation the Oracle then admitted had been a test. [[roll:5|Check the account against the primary assassination record|The Day Of file says the Guild had already moved the body and scrubbed the chambers within hours, and that three guard witnesses were alive on Day 1 — two dead within a fortnight, one vanished. The tableau he describes existed only between the killing and the cleaners, and his one checkable claim is wrong in the direction a reader gets wrong.|The account is internally consistent and contains one detail — the comb — that appears nowhere else in the archive.]]
exhibits.analysis:
## What this testimony is worth

**Two elements are corroborated and therefore add nothing.** That Peach chose her death and left evidence is already in the Day Of record, filed earlier and from a different direction. That the room was managed is also there: body moved within hours, chambers scrubbed, all physical evidence through Guild hands. His agreement is not a second source; it is an echo of a source we already had.

**One element is new.** The comb appears in no other filing. Either it is the detail only a true witness could supply, or it is the specific invented object a constructed scene needs in order to feel witnessed.

**One element is wrong.** He says the responding guards all died. The record says three were alive on Day 1, two dead within two weeks, one vanished — administrative removal over a fortnight, not a massacre in a bedroom. That is the error a person makes reading a casualty list afterwards, not the error a person makes having stood in the room.

**And he cannot be placed there.** He appears in none of the six assassination filings. The Day Of record names fourteen people in and around that palace; he is not among them. By that same record the scene he describes had been erased within hours, so the only people who saw it were the killer, the Guild, or somebody already inside the palace. He implies he is one of the three and never says which.

I am not filing him as a liar. He has never been caught in a falsifiable lie, which is a different and more careful thing. I am filing him as a **source rather than a witness**, and recording that he chose his moment: an audience just proven non-violent, committed, and eighty-five years too young to check.

exhibits.title: Remi Akamatsu's Gehenna Academy student ID
exhibits.secured: surrendered
exhibits.custody: Pierce Anamatar, as the price of passage out of Guild-controlled ground
exhibits.visual:
🪪
Surrendered as payment
Gehenna Academy
no formal withdrawal
exhibits.onRecord: A laminated student identity card issued by Gehenna Academy to Remi Akamatsu, handed to Pierce Anamatar in his den in exchange for passage out of the Skittering Grove. He asked first for the siglet and declined an expired coupon before accepting it, on the stated grounds that it is very durable. [[roll:3|Ask what the card actually proves|Remi left Gehenna without a formal withdrawal, so this was the only document still asserting she had ever been enrolled anywhere. She has no copy.|It reads as a routine student card and a cheap price for three lives.]]
exhibits.analysis:
## Why a man with knights wanted a piece of laminate

Anamatar could have asked for coin, for the battle axe, for the chain shirt Remi had just taken off a corpse. He asked for the **siglet** — a quest object — and when that was not on offer he chose, out of everything in the room, a child's school card. He turned down an expired coupon in between, so he was selecting rather than accepting.

Both of his recorded prices are the same shape: **a thing that belongs to a specific person.** On the Shadow Estate rooftop he took a contract to kill the Oracle in exchange for sending the party home. Here he took the only paper in the grove with Remi's name and an institution on it.

Remi departed Gehenna without withdrawing. That card is the last external evidence that the enrolment happened at all. Whether Anamatar knew that is unestablished, and whether it matters depends entirely on what he does with it.

I am not filing a theory. I am filing that a man who trades in possessions now holds a document that proves who somebody is, and that she handed it over without pausing.

exhibits.onRecord: A heavy box, delivered by Green T, 'from a friend — an associate of the Green Tea Syndicate.' Archie took it from the step, Markop opened it, and Remi was asleep inside. Markop asked who the friend was and Archie answered by stopping in the middle of a word. [[roll:4|Ask who could have put her there|Nobody in the room could say. Green T said he had been gathering backup and that the plan failed 'when no one showed up' — the same hours Remi was out of sight. He does not say he found her.|The box is simply a box. Remi says she sleepwalked, and the table lets that stand.]]
exhibits.analysis:
## Who packs a sleeping child for delivery

The sentence in the record that matters is Green T's: *I've got a delivery from you.* It is addressed to the party and it names a sender the party is not supposed to recognise. Archie recognised it well enough to start saying *dead*.

Three things are established. Green T was away from the cottage when the party rested. He says he was gathering fey, and that nobody came. And whoever packed the box knew where to send it.

What is not established is how Remi got from the far side of Anamatar's passage to a box on a step. Her own account is a theory about sleepwalking. A box that size carried by a man who was elsewhere is not a sleepwalk.

I am not filing a conspiracy. I am filing that the Tea Syndicate was called destroyed in this room, in the same breath, by the man who had just taken delivery from it.

exhibits.title: Archie's half-remembered condition
exhibits.secured: uncorroborated
exhibits.custody: Archie's own account, 1 Aethel, 1040 BF, spoken to Markop in Tymnas's cottage
exhibits.visual:
🕯️
A condition he cannot place
Said once
not repeated
exhibits.onRecord: 'I want to kill the oracle, based on a conversation I had. We kill it or we're stuck here forever. I don't remember the conversation, but I know that if I don't kill the oracle I may never leave here.' Asked why: 'The person who ordered the condition is a jerk.' Markop told him he had left this dimension eight hours ago. Archie said he had thought it was days. [[roll:5|Set it beside the rooftop contract|On the Shadow Estate rooftop a man who trades in possessions took a contract to kill the Oracle in exchange for sending the party home. Archie is describing that contract without its author.|Nothing in the record connects the two. Archie forgot a conversation and no one at the table remembered it for him.]]
exhibits.analysis:
## A debt held by the man who can't spell it

Archie has the terms of a contract and none of the signature. *Kill the oracle or stay.* *The person who ordered the condition is a jerk.* There is only one filed contract in this archive with that shape: Pierce Anamatar's, struck on the Shadow Estate rooftop, kill the Oracle and the party goes home.

The party went home anyway. They went by the Midnight Fountain, lit by Green T, with the Oracle alive and unvisited. Either the contract's condition was never a real gate, or the party left without paying it.

A man who trades in other people's possessions and is owed a death does not have to be in the room to collect. Archie said it himself: he left this dimension eight hours ago and thinks it was days. His sense of what is owed is running on a different clock from everyone else's.

I am not filing a threat. I am filing that Archie chose the ritual over the oracle in one sentence and has not been told what that cost.

investigations.title: Who Signed, And In What
investigations.subtitle: Coronations were theatre; real power signed in blood not ink
investigations.imageCaption: There are a great many images of the capital. Not one of them shows anybody signing anything.
investigations.hook: The Ashford spirit said the coronations were theatre. Waluigi believed him and disliked doing so — and then the Crown Works accountants itemised the scenery.

plainSummary.point: The capital writes everything down except decisions.
plainSummary.detail: Twelve documents, and not one records a person choosing anything. They are stock sheets, transport dockets, rent bills and invoices. The decisions are only visible as the dents they leave in that routine paperwork.

plainSummary.point: A person was moved through the city as cargo.
plainSummary.detail: A restaurant stock sheet lists "exotic stock, one, ambulatory, do not ice" with the price left blank. A prison docket moves an unnamed detainee through three transfers in 31 hours and hands him to a private carriage with no destination written down. A sewer runner's sketch shows both errands crossing at the same junction. Three clerks in three unconnected offices each logged one leg of the same route.

plainSummary.point: One criminal charge is being used as a threat, not a prosecution.
plainSummary.detail: "Consorting with Anomalies" was charged 51 times in eleven years. Nine went to trial. Forty-two were dropped before trial with no reason recorded. In 1040, nineteen were charged and none tried. A charge dropped that often is not meant to convict anyone — it is meant to make people do something.

plainSummary.point: The coronation was staged, and the invoice proves it.
plainSummary.detail: The Crown's own accounts bill for imitation regalia and for a second signing table delivered to a private house. Whatever was really signed was not signed at the public ceremony.

plainSummary.point: Nobody in the capital helps for free.
plainSummary.detail: Every rescue in this file has an unpaid invoice attached to it somewhere. Assume the bill is still outstanding.

plainSummary.point: The Arrangement has a witness now, and he was shot at for it.
plainSummary.detail: A 955 BF account from a ceremonial guard: a Koopa in an unlocked cell shook Fawful's hand with three Mages' Guild hoods watching, a month before the assassination; after a Guild orb put Bowser down to applause, the Chamberlain told the Guild to dispatch of the guard who had seen it. The Guild has his small son and calls it protection. The file holds the night posting, the dead guard's letter to Fawful's bean shop, and the shop's own card.

background.kicker: the crime the capital is still covering up
background.why: The thirty days after Princess Peach's assassination on Highsun 1, 955 BF, with the Regency's cover-up under active construction. Most of the strange paper in this file traces back to that month.

background.kicker: the conspiracy this file is testing
background.why: The alleged coordination between elements of the Regency and the Mages' Guild that let the assassination happen. It rests on Toadsworth the Elder's journals, which the Regency calls forgeries — which is exactly why this file prefers documents to testimony.

background.kicker: the institution behind half the signatures
background.why: Custodians of arcane order, self-appointed. They track individuals with magical badges without always telling them, keep null cages and seem more interested in what the contained can teach them than in whether the containment is ethical. Read this before assuming a Guild signature means oversight.

investigations.brief:
**The short version.** The capital keeps mountains of paperwork and almost none of it records a decision. Twelve documents in this file, and not one of them shows a person choosing something. They show food, transport, rent, charges and stage furniture — and the decisions are visible only as the shapes they leave in those routine records.

That is the finding: **the capital's paperwork is arranged so that the moment of decision never lands in the file of the place it was supposed to happen in.**

Waluigi opened this file expecting the opposite. He wrote at the time that the capital produces speeches while the ruined houses produce evidence, and that the archive would never get a usable sheet of paper out of it. That was wrong, and the archive would rather record a retraction than quietly stop mentioning it. The capital produces enormous quantities of usable paper. It simply never writes down the part you want.

## What this file is arguing

Twelve exhibits, and the argument they make together is one sentence: *the capital's machinery is built so that the decisive act never appears in the record of the place where it was supposed to happen.*

Take them in the order the archive filed them.

A restaurant stock sheet has four lines of food with prices and a fifth line — **exotic stock, one, ambulatory, do not ice** — with the cost column blank. An Imperial movement docket takes an unnamed detainee through three transfers in thirty-one hours and releases him to a private carriage with no destination entered. A runner's sketch shows two unrelated errands crossing at the same junction under the lower capital, which means the sewers are not an escape route, they are a **corridor with regular traffic**.

Then the charges. Fifty-one Consorting with Anomalies charges laid in eleven years; nine tried; forty-two withdrawn before trial with no reason given. In the early years every charge went to trial and every trial convicted. In 1040 nineteen have been laid and none have been tried at all. And the wanted bill for Markop's father exists in two printings from the same plate, four years apart, with the charge line cut out of the block and reset half a point high — false witness, then consorting with anomalies. Same man, same reward, same plate, **new offence**.

A charge that is laid and then withdrawn forty-two times out of fifty-one is not a prosecution. It is an instrument, and the archive would like to know what it is used to obtain, since it is plainly not used to obtain convictions.

## The Ashford problem, stated honestly

The spirit said the coronations were theatre and that real power *signed in blood not ink*. That testimony is the reason this file exists and Waluigi has spent the whole investigation trying not to lean on it.

It is one copy of one account of one conversation, transcribed by a third party in a hand resembling Luigi's, unauthenticated, with no second hearer produced. As evidence it is close to worthless and the archive files it that way.

Which is why the Crown Works account matters more than the testimony does. Eighteen hundred and twenty-five gold for a dais, standards, gilt-over-base-metal display regalia, carriage and night working, settled in full with no query raised. And ninety-five gold for a **second signing table**, charged as a rehearsal item and delivered to a private address rather than the hall.

Waluigi did not need a spirit to say the ceremony was staged. The Crown's own accountants itemised the staging, priced the fake regalia, and then billed for a signing table that went somewhere else.

That is the standing rule of this archive working exactly as intended: an unfalsifiable claim from an interested witness, corroborated in the least glamorous way available, by somebody in an office who was only trying to get paid.

## What is still missing

The iron beneath the hanging tree has not been recovered and the survey sheets do not help as much as the file would like. A feature annotated *hanging tree* on the 1021 sheet, with a margin note about compasses; open ground on the 1038 sheet; no felling recorded between them. That is a discrepancy, not a location, and the archive is not going to pretend otherwise.

Waluigi's assessment: the succession thread will not be settled by finding the iron. It will be settled by finding out who withdraws the forty-two charges, because that person is the one deciding what never reaches a courtroom, and this file has now established that they exist, that they have been at it for eleven years, and that they have stopped bothering with trials altogether.

WAH.

threads.title: Documents sealed in iron beneath a hanging tree
threads.text:
Coordinates in the Thornwood, per the Ashford testimony. Still unrecovered — but the survey sheets now put a *hanging tree* on the 1021 sheet with a margin note about unreliable compasses, and open ground on the 1038 sheet, with **no felling recorded between them**. That is a discrepancy rather than a location, and the archive will not upgrade it until somebody walks the ground.

**In plain terms:** two survey sheets disagree about whether a tree exists, and no one logged cutting it down. That is a gap in the paperwork, not a map reference — the archive is not going to dress it up as a location until somebody physically walks the ground.

threads.title: Consorting with Anomalies is an instrument, not an offence
threads.text:
Fifty-one laid in eleven years, nine tried, forty-two withdrawn before trial with no reason given. Early years: every charge tried, every trial convicted. 1040: nineteen laid, none tried. And Kaelor's wanted bill was reprinted from the same plate with the charge line cut out and reset. Whoever withdraws the forty-two is deciding what never reaches a courtroom.

**In plain terms:** a charge dropped forty-two times out of fifty-one is not being used to convict anyone. It is being used to make people do something else. Find whoever signs the withdrawals and you find the person deciding what never reaches a courtroom.

threads.title: People leave the capital as freight
threads.text:
*Exotic stock, one, ambulatory, do not ice* on a restaurant stock sheet with the cost column blank; an Imperial docket releasing a detainee to a private carriage at the goods gate with no destination entered; and a sewer sketch where two unrelated errands cross at the same junction. Three separate clerks describing one route without knowing it.

**In plain terms:** three clerks in three unconnected offices — a kitchen, a prison, a sewer runner — each wrote down one leg of the same route without realising. People are being moved out of the capital as cargo, and the cargo paperwork is the only record of it.

threads.title: The signing did not happen where the ceremony did
threads.text:
The Crown Works account prices the dais, the standards and three sets of gilt-over-base-metal display regalia — and then bills ninety-five gold for a **second signing table**, charged as a rehearsal item and delivered to a private address. The Ashford spirit's claim that the coronations were theatre is corroborated by the people who invoiced for the scenery.

**In plain terms:** the Crown's own accountants billed for fake regalia and a spare signing table sent to a private house. Whatever was actually signed was not signed at the ceremony, and the invoice proves it more reliably than the ghost does.

threads.title: Every rescue in this file was billed to somebody
threads.text:
Three hundred gold for *compounding under duress*, invented on the spot by the Mages' Guild and never received. An inert dragon scale traded for six bags of spotted mushrooms with both parties recorded as satisfied. An empty canister returned with a prisoner whose kit was supposedly removed on entry. The capital does not refuse assistance; it prices it and then argues about the invoice.

**In plain terms:** nobody in the capital refuses to help. They help, then invoice, then argue about the invoice. Treat every rescue in this file as a transaction with an unpaid balance somewhere.

threads.title: The Arrangement has a corridor now — and the Guild was loved first
threads.text: Until this session the Arrangement was a dead chamberlain's disputed handwriting. Now it is a corridor with people in it: a Koopa out of an unlocked cell, Fawful's hand in his, three Mages' Guild hoods saying the Guild is already in place and will not act yet, and — a quarter of an hour later, in a hall that had just cheered the Guild for putting Bowser down with one orb — the Chamberlain telling the Guild to dispatch of the only witness. The thread is the order of those events. The Guild did not seize the castle. It was applauded into it, and the first thing the applause bought was a kill order nobody in the hall objected to. The journals say *the Guild provided the method, the Regency provided the opportunity*. The account shows the method being cheered and the opportunity being spoken aloud, a month early, by a man in a new suit.

leads.title: Recover the documents sealed in iron
leads.objective: Locate the hanging tree in the Thornwood and retrieve whatever is sealed beneath it in iron. Start from the 1021 survey sheet, not the 1038 one, and take a second compass.
leads.why: It is the only physical evidence the succession thread has ever been offered, and it was offered by a spirit whose other statements are unfalsifiable. Two survey sheets seventeen years apart now disagree about whether the tree exists, with no felling recorded between them, which is either a cartographic error or somebody editing the map. Iron and paper are falsifiable. Go and get them.

leads.title: Identify the third branch
leads.objective: Establish which branch of the succession the Ashford spirit meant by “broken at third branch,” and whether the break was an event or a procedure.
leads.why: Held against the Aurelian grafting page, *branch* stops being a genealogist's metaphor and becomes the same gardening vocabulary the Feyward uses for splicing a bloodline. If the capital's succession was grafted, the crisis has a mechanism instead of a mystery.

leads.title: Name whoever withdraws the Anomalies charges
leads.objective: Obtain the withdrawal instruments for any of the forty-two charges discontinued before trial and read the signature block. One will do.
leads.why: Forty-two of fifty-one charges withdrawn without reason given, and nineteen laid in 1040 with none tried at all. Whoever signs the discontinuances decides what never reaches a courtroom, and this file has established that they exist and have been at it for eleven years. A charge used forty-two times and prosecuted nine is not a prosecution; it is a lever with a handle, and the handle has a name on it.

leads.title: Trace the goods-gate carriage
leads.objective: Identify the private carriage that took an unnamed Toad detainee out of the goods gate at 22:05 with no destination entered, and the clerk of the Chamberlain who authorised the movement at 21:40.
leads.why: The docket, the restaurant stock sheet and the sewer route card were made by three people who did not know each other and describe one route between them. That route is still open. Eager came back off it; the archive has no reason to believe he was the only person on it, and the stock sheet's cost column is blank because somebody else was paying.

leads.title: Settle or contest the Mages' Guild bill before it is assigned
leads.objective: Either pay the eight hundred and seventy, or challenge the three hundred gold charged for *compounding under duress* as a line item with no tariff behind it. Do one of them in writing.
leads.why: An unpaid bill is a debt and a debt is transferable. The Guild invented that charge on the spot with an Archmage standing over a bench, which makes it contestable — but only while it is still the Guild's to contest. Once it is sold on, the party is arguing with a purchaser who was not in the room and does not care.

leads.title: Find out what is in the fat vial, and who filled it
leads.objective: Trace the vial the Koopa prisoner carried from the dungeon to the Bean Badge — through the shop card's 'bring the vial', Fawful's own description of the vacuum shroom going into Bowser by way of it, and any Guild or Beanish apothecary record of a vessel built to dose a Koopa King.
leads.why: The vial is the one object in the night that was built to go into somebody, it was on the Koopa's errand list before Bowser came through the wall, and the Highsun 1 record has Bowser dragged across a corridor unconscious a month later with nobody asking why he went down so easily. If the vial was used, the official murderer of Highsun 1 was dosed by the people who later accused him, and that moves the file from 'who held the blade' to 'who held the Koopa King'.

leads.title: Establish which Toadsworth gave the Guild the dispatch order — and why the brothers did nothing
leads.objective: Put a second account beside John Lee's for the hall after the orb: who stood where, which Toadsworth spoke, what Mario and Luigi were doing when a hood loosed a bolt at a ceremonial guard in front of them.
leads.why: The account calls the man 'the chancellor' and the archive reads him as the Chamberlain; the whole Loyalist case against Toadsworth the Elder would change weight if the son said it, and the Regency's defence of the Elder would collapse if a second witness puts the words in the father's mouth. And two heroes watched a kill order given and obeyed. Either they did not hear it, or Highsun 1 was not the first night the brothers were in the wrong place with permission.

leads.title: Name the dead guard with the bean shop's address in his coat
leads.objective: Match the palace guard who died in Bowser's fire with the letter in his livery against the palace roll for Efferd 955, the Regency's casualty list for the incursion, and the Bean Badge card's 'the guard' who had not decided.
leads.why: If the hall had one Toad holding the Arrangement's address it had more than one, and a name turns 'the castle was full of it' from Waluigi's reading into a roster. It also tells the file whether the Arrangement recruited palace guards or planted paper on them, which decides how much of the forty-seven minutes on Highsun 1 was consent.

leads.title: Find out how the Guild came to have Toad Lee, and where Marilyn went
leads.objective: Account for the small boy between the dining-hall table past midnight — with the chambermaid Marilyn — and the Guild's dawn statement that his son was 'being taken care of' and would not have to worry about being trafficked in their care; find the maid.
leads.why: The Guild volunteered the word 'trafficked' about a child it was holding, unasked, to a father it had shot at. A custody chain for the boy is a custody chain for the one hostage the Arrangement is on record taking, and the boy grew up to be a member of Disaster Inc. whose own file already has a lead open on his missing time. The maid is the last person on the record with him before the Guild, and nobody has asked her anything because nobody has found her.
